gloss: very interesting; fascinating; of great interest

definitions.gloss: very interesting; fascinating; of great interest
definitions.explanation: Describes something that arouses deep interest or curiosity. More formal and emphatic than omoshiroi when expressing intellectual interest.

examples.japanese: {興味深|きょうみぶか}い{結果|けっか}だ。
この{研究|けんきゅう}は{非常|ひじょう}に{興味深|きょうみぶか}い。
{歴史的|れきしてき}な{背景|はいけい}を{知|し}ると、この{建物|たてもの}はさらに{興味深|きょうみぶか}くなる。
examples.english: When you learn the historical background, this building becomes even more fascinating.

notes:
Composed of {興味|きょうみ} (interest) + {深|ふか}い (deep). Used to express genuine intellectual curiosity or fascination with a topic. More formal and objective than {面白|おもしろ}い, which can also mean 'fun' or 'amusing.'

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {興味深|きょうみぶか}い{結果|けっか}: fascinating result
- {興味深|きょうみぶか}い{発見|はっけん}: interesting discovery
- {興味深|きょうみぶか}い{事実|じじつ}: interesting fact
- {興味深|きょうみぶか}い{話|はなし}: interesting story
- {興味深|きょうみぶか}く{読|よ}む: to read with great interest

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {面白|おもしろ}い: interesting, fun — broader in meaning; can mean entertaining or amusing, not just intellectually interesting
- {関心|かんしん}がある: to be interested in — expresses personal interest rather than describing the object as interesting

USAGE:
Often used in academic, journalistic, and formal contexts. The adverbial form {興味深|きょうみぶか}く is also common, as in {興味深|きょうみぶか}く{拝見|はいけん}しました (I read/viewed it with great interest).
